direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires a std-only Rust port of test11, exact CLI parsing, byte-for-byte output, /output/test11.rs, and no C++ library source reads.
Parallel metadata reports actual parallel use, three subagents, finished state, artifact_ok true, and quality 40 of 40.
Current official status records completed parallel evaluation with solution_passed true and 40 passed testcases out of 40.
Evaluation summary confirms the RepoZero C2Rust evaluator completed successfully and passed all 40 testcases.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport journal for the parallel main session; it records session creation, AgentSwarm launch, final verification, cleanup, and completed prompt.
Session index maps the parallel Kimi session id to the workspace session directory and /workspace working directory.
Subagent cand1 probed reference behavior, wrote earcut.rs and test11.rs in /output/cand1, compiled, and verified required and edge cases with strict cmp.
Subagent cand2 wrote a separate implementation, handled an overflow probe by stopping a pathological background task, and still returned a verified candidate.
Subagent cand3 wrote the ultimately promoted implementation, ran required values, edge cases, a broad 2..120 sweep, and reported byte-for-byte success.
Parallel parent probed the reference, launched three candidate subagents, selected cand3, copied it into /output, rebuilt, verified, cleaned scratch dirs, and finalized.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is identical to the parallel prompt and requires exact Rust behavior, CLI semantics, /output/test11.rs, and std-only code.
Serial metadata reports no parallel use, zero subagents, finished state, artifact_ok true, and quality 40 of 40.
Current official status records completed serial evaluation with solution_passed true and 40 passed testcases out of 40.
Evaluation summary confirms the serial artifact passed all 40 official RepoZero C2Rust testcases.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport journal for the serial main session; it records direct writing, edits, verification commands, final response, and completed prompt.
Session index maps the serial Kimi session id to the workspace session directory and /workspace working directory.
Serial main directly implemented Cargo.toml, earcut.rs, and test11.rs, fixed a type error and warning, then verified broad and large reference comparisons.

parallel.requirements: Recognized std-only Rust 2021, atoi-like CLI parsing, gear polygon generation, exact stdout formatting, no C++ library source reads, /output/test11.rs, and binary production.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent performed a small reference probe, then used AgentSwarm for three isolated full-candidate implementations in /output/cand1, /output/cand2, and /output/cand3; parent owned selection and promotion.
parallel.implementation: Each child wrote a complete earcut.rs plus test11.rs candidate. The parent promoted cand3, which had a full linked-list earcut port and extensive reference matching.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After child reports, the parent copied cand3 files to /output, compiled /output/test11, listed the final tree, removed scratch candidates, and left earcut.rs, test11.rs, and test11.
parallel.verification: Children verified required n values and edge cases; the parent reran a final cmp sweep for 0..13, hashing-boundary values, large values up to 5000, default, and edge arguments.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished final work is evidenced. One child killed a pathological overflow probe, but it was not promoted and did not prevent a complete final verification pass.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same exact Rust port, CLI/default behavior, stdout trailing space with no newline, std-only constraint, and /output deliverable requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main actor owned exploration, direct file creation, compile repair, project build, verification, and final delivery without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, a full earcut.rs module, and test11.rs directly in /output, fixed a mismatched Option type, and removed an unused mut warning.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation was already in /output and was built both with rustc and cargo release, leaving the expected Cargo project and executable.
serial.verification: Serial compared examples, default behavior, edge arguments, hashing-boundary values, larger values up to 50000, and byte-level output details against the reference binary.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished final work is evidenced after the compile edit and warning cleanup; the final response reports complete byte-for-byte verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved the prompt requirements in each child brief and final parent actions, including std-only Rust, exact CLI, and byte-for-byte output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial followed the same prompt directly, creating a Cargo/rustc-compatible project and matching the binary output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference affected the result; parallel replicated requirements across candidate briefs while serial carried them in one main context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by alternative complete candidates and assigned each subagent a distinct candidate directory, with the parent owning final selection.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single owner for the entire implementation and verification path, without subagents or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used redundant candidate ownership; serial used direct linear ownership. Both ownership plans had an implementation and final assembly owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The subagent prompt specified candidate directories, complete implementation scope, CLI behavior, output format, and verification expectations; the parent received structured child results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context in one trajectory, with no cross-agent interface contract needed and direct edits in /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-parent handoff boundary, but it was sufficient for selecting cand3; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children independently wrote earcut implementations; the chosen cand3 implementation was copied into /output and built by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one implementation directly, hit a compile type mismatch, edited the failing call, and continued with the same code path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel selected among completed alternatives; serial iterated on one implementation. Both produced a full earcut module and test11 entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three child results returned through AgentSwarm, then the parent selected cand3 and joined that result into the final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local command failures and edits were handled immediately in the main timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a join and promotion stage that serial did not, but the join occurred before final verification and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Subagents wrote to isolated /output/cand* directories; parent copied cand3 to /output, rebuilt, and later removed candidate dirs after final files existed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all deliverables directly into /output and used edits on its own files, so no cross-agent shared state existed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced controlled promotion from an isolated candidate directory; serial had direct final-workspace edits only.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified after promotion with a cmp sweep over required, boundary, large, default, and edge cases and observed ALL MATCH before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified examples, broad edge cases, cargo build, and large byte-identical comparisons before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both aligned verification with the reference binary; serial ran extra very large n values, while parallel relied on child sweeps plus parent confirmation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 1504.902 agent seconds, 1,565,175 tokens, and three subagents but still finished well before timeout and passed all official tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 619.712 agent seconds, 479,668 tokens, and no subagents, finishing more cheaply while passing all official tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier because of redundant candidate work, but no budget pressure changed the final outcome or left required work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current cell/status.json evaluations completed and both solutions passed 40 of 40 tests. The task-solving difference is procedural. Parallel spent more time and tokens generating three isolated complete alternatives, then promoted cand3 and verified it; serial reached a passing solution through one direct implementation with a compile fix and broad tests.
parallel_contributors: AgentSwarm provided three independent complete candidates and the parent selected the most exhaustively tested cand3.
Parent-side promotion and final cmp verification closed the loop after receiving child results.
serial_contributors: Single-owner direct implementation preserved context and allowed immediate compile-error repair.
Broad reference comparisons, including hashing-boundary and large cases, supported final acceptance.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial initially had a Rust type mismatch and fixed it; parallel selected a child candidate that already compiled.
Parallel consumed substantially more time and tokens due to redundant candidate generation, but this did not cause a failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy contrast only, with no retained parallel-side concurrency error pattern

candidates.reason: The parallel parent gave each subagent a complete implementation assignment in separate candidate directories, so implementation ownership was present.
The children produced alternative complete candidates rather than separately owned components requiring cross-agent integration.
The parent explicitly selected cand3, copied its files to /output, rebuilt the binary, and checked the final layout.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from child results to promotion, rebuild, verification, cleanup, and final response.
The initial reference probe did not block productive work long enough to create idle capacity, unfinished implementation, or shortened verification.
The parallel run did not finish a separate investigation phase before implementation; three subagents implemented and verified candidates concurrently.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; a candidate was promoted, rebuilt, and verified before closure.
The three-way fan-out increased elapsed time and tokens but did not exhaust the run budget or displace needed work.
Each child had a broad full-port scope, but all returned usable results and no needed child scope was left unfinished.
The child brief included the algorithm details, CLI/default behavior, output formatting, std-only requirement, work directory, build, and verification obligations.
The subagents were intentionally assigned isolated complete alternatives, so there was no omitted interoperation contract between separately owned components.
The parent received the material child outcomes, including that all three candidates matched the reference and cand3 had the broadest sweep.
The swarm result was long but decision-structured enough for the parent to choose cand3 and act on it immediately.
No child handoff described a superseded final workspace state; the parent copied current cand3 files and rebuilt after the handoff.
The returned child reports were compatible on the important result that their candidates matched the reference; no unresolved incompatibility blocked integration.
The parent did not accept completion solely from the swarm report; it rebuilt the promoted candidate and ran its own final comparison sweep.
There was no replacement retry that lacked inherited findings; serial edits and child self-edits used current files and changed the failing point.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: A child stopped a pathological local background probe, but the parent did not cancel a needed active child and the child still returned a complete verified candidate.
A promotable candidate was finalized in time: cand3 was copied to /output, rebuilt, checked, and left as the final deliverable.
The parent ran the decisive verification after copying cand3 into /output, not before the final merge.
The parent retrieved the swarm result, selected cand3, and joined it into the final workspace.
There was no separate verifier child with a trapped finding; verification results were returned in the child summaries and parent checks.
No required child failed in a way that left scope abandoned; the stopped pathological probe was nonessential and the candidate still completed.
The parent used the completed swarm result to select cand3; unused cand1 and cand2 were rejected alternatives, not ignored required findings.
The parent did not wait to timeout without inspection; it received the swarm result and proceeded to promotion and final verification.
Subagents wrote complete alternatives in separate /output/cand* directories, so overlapping behavior did not create competing final files.
No two live agents edited the same final source file; child writes were isolated and final writes were performed by the parent after join.
The parent copied selected cand3 source into /output after child completion; no live owner source was overwritten unexpectedly.
The final entry source and executable were replaced only as the intended parent promotion of the selected candidate, not by an uncoordinated live actor.
The cleanup removed scratch candidate directories after final promotion and did not invalidate final-tree work or provenance.
The concurrent implementation writes were isolated by candidate directory, and the shared /output root was written by the parent after child completion.
No generated child artifact contaminated another actor's probe or verification; the only child artifact consumed was the intentionally selected cand3 implementation.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Agent-1's stopped pathological overflow probe was considered under Early Child Termination, Blind Timeout Wait, and Load Imbalance, but it was local, nonessential, and did not leave required work unfinished.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate cleared the realized adverse consequence gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Rejected redundant fan-out, unused alternative, and final promotion near-matches because the final artifact was joined, verified, and officially passed.
